questions.a_label_rule_fail_open: YES - a document can be served and labelled verified_input while the period the plan demands is absent. Constructed case (b06_review_probe.json#claim4_no_fiscal_year): sidecar with no fiscal_year/period_end and the year removed from the title, filing_date kept so the handle stays capture_ready; request with fiscal_year=None. resolve -> reused_exact, 1 match, handle.fiscal_year=None, handle.published_date='2026-02-20', capture_ready=True; envelope qualification = {label: verified_input, gaps: [], reason: ''}. Same in mode=latest_as_of (where the consumer contract FORBIDS fiscal_year). b06-plan.md section 2 defines '期间' as fiscal_year AND (period_end OR published_date) and section 4 lists '期间不明（无 fiscal_year ...）=> blocked + period_missing'; the implementation (resolver.py _qualification_gaps) and its test (test_r4b06_unknown_period_blocks_the_formal_contract, line 243-245: 'a published date alone still counts as a known period') assert the opposite. Net effect: period_missing can never appear for a served handle (resolve.py:1397-1399 refuses a document with no published_date), so the period half of 'identity + period + source complete' is vacuous. Counter-argument recorded honestly: b-design.md B06 never defines '期间'; a published date is a period fact; and in latest_as_of the caller has no year by contract - so the fix may legitimately be to amend the plan instead of the code. See B-VR06-01.
questions.b_weaker_licence_inherited: YES - nothing except the new field signals anything but success. Measured on the conflict fixture with a real bundle (b06_review_probe.json#claim2b_blocked_looks_like_success): qualification={label: blocked, gaps: [], reason: 'field conflict recorded for: title'} while outcome='reused_existing', download_events=0, bundle_status='available' with a bundle_hash, prompt_injection_status='not_reviewed', handle.capture_ready=True with missing_capture_fields=[]. The consumer's validator accepts the envelope and its permission gate (revenue-forecast/scripts/company_wiki_source.py:280-281) only tests handle.capture_ready - a conflict-blocked handle is capture_ready, so the gate passes; grep shows no consumer reads 'qualification' at all (filing-fetch and revenue-forecast). A missing qualification is not the failure mode: build_resolution_envelope sets it whenever resolution.matches is non-empty (verified). The design sentence requiring the consumer gate to align with the label is undelivered and unregistered (S-4 moves consumer work to phase C, but test-acceptance-map.md carries no not_verified marking; the string 'not_verified' does not appear in that file). See B-VR06-05.
questions.c_claim3_exact: Mostly, but not exactly. Same column (documents.metadata_json), same reserved key constant (scanner.R4_PROVENANCE_KEY, imported not copied), same conflict predicate (record is a dict and record.get('conflicts') is truthy) - so for well-formed content the two agree, measured on the same document (envelope blocked / read side metadata_status='blocked'). They disagree in two reachable-by-a-caller situations: (1) malformed shared-column content - the read side raises (AttributeError for fields as a list, JSONDecodeError for invalid JSON) while B06 answers '' and the envelope says verified_input, i.e. the two are not the same fact there, and B06's answer is the fail-open one; (2) store omitted/None - build_resolution_envelope(res, store=None) labels the very same document verified_input while the read side (and the store-supplied envelope) says blocked (b06_review_probe.json#claim3_store_none_label). A consumer sees whichever artefact it reads: the CLI resolve/ensure responses embed the envelope, so a consumer of the envelope sees qualification; the read side is a separate API (query_filing_candidates) that no consumer currently calls through the envelope. The read-side crash on a malformed column is a pre-existing B05 defect, not introduced by B06, but the 'same fact, not a second opinion' claim does not cover it. See B-VR06-02.
questions.d_preview_reachable: NO path found, and I looked for one. Probed: SourceResolver.resolve (missing URL -> MISSING/capture_incomplete/qualification None), all three build_resolution_envelope call sites (cli resolve, cli ensure, close_gap - all fed by resolve), reader.resolve_handle/bundle (no envelope), and the public builder itself. The only way to obtain label='preview' is to hand build_resolution_envelope a ResolutionResult whose handle was doctored (dataclasses.replace(handle, https_url=None, missing_capture_fields=('https_url',))), which no in-package code can produce: ResolutionResult has exactly one constructor (resolver.py:1894) and the unique producer refuses not handle.capture_ready at resolver.py:1466. The same argument kills identity_missing / period_missing / source_missing on the production path: missing_capture_fields is always empty for a served handle, published_date is required to be served, and document_entities always has at least one row because scanner.py:1026-1033 inserts an entity for every document it indexes (falling back to f'unresolved:{root_id}'); scanner.py is the ONLY writer of documents/document_entities in the package (verified by grep over src). identity_missing does fire on the envelope when the DB is put into a state the pipeline never creates - deleting the entity rows on a TEMP catalog produced label blocked/gaps ['identity_missing'] with the document still served (b06_review_probe.json#claim4_identity_db_surgery).

g_sampled_commits.CFG-08_728b5e0: Rule consistent with the annotations: RootSpec declares read_only: bool = True (config.py:137 item.get('read_only', True)) and reusable_for_filing: bool | None = None ('None = follow kind policy'); the new _require_boolean refuses a present null for read_only and still admits null for reusable_for_filing; absent fields skip so their defaults apply. Measured pre/post (b06_review_cfg08_pre.json / _head.json, config.py swapped to the 728b5e0^ blob): pre-fix `read_only:` (null) was refused by RootSpec.__post_init__ with a raw TypeError('read_only must be a boolean') (models.py:147-148, present before this commit) and post-fix it is refused by the admission point with CatalogConfigError('...CFG-08'); `read_only: "false"` is CatalogConfigError in both; `reusable_for_filing:` (null) is accepted with None in both. So the rule now matches the annotations - but the reason recorded in the commit message, the config.py comment and the new test docstring ('a present-but-empty value is refused instead of being stored as None - which is falsy, while the absent field's default is True') is not what the old code did: a null was never stored, it raised TypeError. The B03 review's own finding (B-VR03-03) stated the mechanism correctly; only the new wording overstates it. See B-VR06-08.
g_sampled_commits.B03_dispositions_2f1ddab: All three reproduced red -> green with direct probes (b06_review_b03_pre.json = resolver.py from 2f1ddab^, b06_review_b03_head.json = HEAD). (1) commonpath containment: pre volumes-root case _inside_configured_roots(file_on_C:, root=Path('C:\\')) = false (the prefix bug: base + os.sep becomes 'c:\\\\'), post = true; sibling-with-shared-prefix stays false, the root itself stays true, a different drive stays false via the ValueError branch. (2) pinned expected_content_sha256: with the handle naming version A and the file on disk holding version B, calling read_verified_bytes(handle, expected_content_sha256=<hash of B on disk>) returned status 'verified' with the bytes and reported content_sha256 = B's hash BEFORE, and status 'unavailable' reason 'expected_version_mismatch' with no bytes AFTER - i.e. the P1 scenario (one version's document_id beside another version's bytes while calling itself verified) is really closed. (3) cancellation tail guard: with a budget that cancels only on the 4th read of .cancelled (the check after the final b''-returning read), the pre code returned the bytes (only 3 accesses existed) and the post code returns unavailable/'cancelled' with no bytes (4 accesses). The reviewer-independent claim 'the tail guard is needed' is therefore confirmed, not merely asserted.

findings.claim: The delivered label rule is not the rule the run registered for the period: 'verified_input' is emitted for a served document that has no fiscal_year, while b06-plan.md defines the period as fiscal_year AND (period_end OR published_date) and lists 'no fiscal_year' as blocked/period_missing. period_missing is therefore unreachable for any served handle and the period component of 'identity + period + source complete' is vacuous.
findings.evidence: b06_review_probe.json#claim4_no_fiscal_year (exact mode with fiscal_year=None: reused_exact, handle.fiscal_year=None, handle.published_date='2026-02-20', qualification {verified_input, [], ''}; identical in latest_as_of, the mode in which filing-fetch FORBIDS fiscal_year). Code: resolver.py _qualification_gaps requires only 'fiscal_year is None AND no published_date' - and resolve refuses a document with no published_date (resolver.py:1397-1399), so the branch can never fire. The delivered test asserts the relaxation explicitly (test_r4b06_qualification.py:243-245), and mutation M11 (making the code conform to the plan) is killed by that test, so the divergence is intentional but unregistered. Reachable entry points: the resolve CLI's --fiscal-year is optional (cli.py:417) and SourceRequest.fiscal_year is nullable (resolver.py:487).
findings.impact: A caller (or consumer in latest_as_of, which is forbidden from sending fiscal_year) can receive a response whose qualification asserts a complete period for a document whose fiscal period is not established by its own facts - the fail-open direction the design's 'period unknown => blocked' rule exists to prevent. It also means the F-B01-7 acceptance item registered on the B06 row has no reachable trigger (see B-VR06-04).
findings.required_action: Decide and make the two records agree: either (a) treat 'no fiscal_year' as period_missing/blocked (restore the plan's rule; the delivered test must then be corrected), or (b) keep published_date as a sufficient period and record the relaxation in b06-plan.md section 2/4 with the reason, so the rule and its evidence match. Also register the F-B01-7 carrier question explicitly (the xfail in revenue-forecast/tests/test_fc1001_isolated_lake.py will not XPASS on B06).

findings.claim: 'The same fact the read side reports as metadata_status=blocked, not a second opinion' holds only for well-formed metadata_json; when the conflict evidence is unreadable or not supplied, the envelope reports the STRONGEST label (verified_input) instead of the read side's blocked (or its hard failure).
findings.evidence: b06_review_probe.json#claim3_read_side_agreement#malformed_shared_column: for '{"r4_provenance": {"fields": []}}' and for a list-of-pairs fields value the read side raises AttributeError("'list' object has no attribute 'items'") while _metadata_conflict_reason returns '' and the envelope label is verified_input; for invalid JSON the read side raises JSONDecodeError and B06 again says verified_input. #claim3_store_none_label: with store=None the same conflicted document yields qualification verified_input while the store-supplied envelope (and query_filing_candidates) says blocked. Evidence direction is fail-open, and the malformed-column read side failure is a pre-existing B05 defect, so the two artefacts do not describe one fact in those states.
findings.impact: A consumer holding an envelope built without a store, or built while the shared column is damaged, sees a clean 'verified_input' for a document the read side calls blocked (or cannot read at all). No in-package caller omits the store today, but build_resolution_envelope is public API and the FC-704/FC-902 suites call it without one.
findings.required_action: Make absence of conflict evidence visible rather than green: either distinguish 'no evidence' from 'no conflict' in the label (e.g. a gaps code such as conflict_evidence_unavailable) or refuse/soften the label when store is None; and record the malformed-column asymmetry with the read side (which still raises) as a known divergence, since B06 explicitly reasoned about that column's shape.

findings.claim: The acceptance suite does not pin the wiring of the identity/period/source gaps into the response: a mutant that keeps the conflict read but never applies _qualification_gaps in build_resolution_envelope survives the entire targeted set.
findings.evidence: RUN/evidence/b06_review_mutations.json (M6 survived the B06 file) and RUN/evidence/b06_review_m6.json (M6 survived all six targeted files: 50 passed; the temp tree's resolver.py blob was verified identical to HEAD before and after the run). The mutant is the fail-open direction - every capture-ready handle keeps gaps=[].
findings.impact: The claim 'blocked when identity/period/source are unknown' is enforced only at rule level; a future edit that stops calling the rule (or reorders it) would not turn any test red even though it changes the response contract.
findings.required_action: Add one envelope-level case per blocking code exercised through the public builder (an unambiguous way to do it without touching the cross-repo gate: build the ResolutionResult via dataclasses.replace on a real handle, as the rule-level cases already do, but assert through build_resolution_envelope(...).to_dict()), so at least identity_missing and source_missing are pinned on the response path.

findings.claim: The implementation record classifies the identity/period/source blocking cases as reachable via the real resolve plus envelope assertions, but they are rule-level only, and no catalog the pipeline can produce reaches them: the reachable label surface is verified_input and blocked-by-conflict alone.
findings.evidence: b06-implementation.md section 4 ('reachable path' list includes _unknown_identity/_unknown_period/_missing_source), while the test bodies for those three do dataclasses.replace(handle, ...) and call _qualification_gaps/_qualification_label directly (test file lines 216-270); only complete_handle, missing_url, unanswered_request and field_conflict go through a real resolve. Probes: #claim4_missing_url (missing URL -> refusal, qualification None), #claim4_no_fiscal_year (no year -> verified_input), #claim4_identity_from_scan (a sidecar with canonical_entity_id=None still yields entity row 'ticker:ACME' because _entity() derives it from the path; scanner.py:1026-1033 inserts an entity for EVERY indexed document and scanner.py is the only writer of documents/document_entities in the package), #claim4_identity_db_surgery (identity_missing fires on the envelope only after deleting the entity rows in a TEMP catalog - a state the pipeline never creates). F-B01-7's registered half ('identity unknown => blocked') therefore has no reachable trigger on any indexed state, which is consistent with the author's own note that the revenue xfail will not XPASS.
findings.impact: Reviewers and the owner may read 'blocked covers identity/period/source' as delivered behaviour when only one of the four blocking triggers (a real field conflict) can actually occur today. The F-B01-7 acceptance item stays open under B06 while appearing covered.
findings.required_action: Correct the classification in b06-implementation.md section 4 (rule-level vs reachable) and state the reachable surface explicitly in the B06 acceptance row, including that the F-B01-7 item is NOT delivered by B06 (as b06-plan.md section 5 already argues) so the map does not read as covered.

findings.claim: The design requires the consumer's existing permission gate to align with the qualification label; B06 delivers the fact only, and neither the acceptance map nor the implementation record registers the undelivered half as not_verified.
findings.evidence: b-design.md B06: 'requires the consumer existing permission gate (revenue-forecast/scripts/company_wiki_source.py:280-281 capture_ready) to align with it - B only provides facts, does not change consumers'. Measured (b06_review_probe.json#claim2b_blocked_looks_like_success): a conflict-blocked response still carries outcome=reused_existing, download_events=0, bundle_status=available, prompt_injection_status=not_reviewed and a capture_ready handle, so company_wiki_source.record_source's gate passes; grep shows neither filing-fetch nor revenue-forecast reads 'qualification'; test-acceptance-map.md contains no not_verified marking (owner decision S-4 requires the consumer side to be marked not_verified in B's acceptance record, and the B06 row lists only L09/L10 and the F-B01-7 item).
findings.impact: The S-13 deliverable - a response-level blocked a consumer can act on - is currently unobservable to the only existing consumer, so 'blocked' behaves like success for anyone who does not read the new field. Nothing in the B06 record tells phase C what it must now enforce.
findings.required_action: Register on the B06 row that the consumer-side alignment is NOT delivered and mark it not_verified (consumer licence gate must check qualification.label before accepting a handle), so the C phase inherits an explicit requirement instead of an implied one.

findings.claim: For a multi-match (AMBIGUOUS) response the envelope qualifies matches[0] and can therefore carry label 'verified_input' on a response that is not a single verified input.
findings.evidence: resolver.py:1488-1505 returns AMBIGUOUS with matches=tuple(exact) (>1 handle); build_resolution_envelope qualifies matches[0] unconditionally; probe #claim4_two_matches_label: an envelope built from a two-match resolution reports {label: verified_input, gaps: [], reason: ''}. outcome stays 'ambiguous', which is why this is P3 rather than worse.
findings.impact: A consumer that reads qualification without outcome could read an ambiguous answer as a verified input. The design does not define the label for zero/multiple handles, so the choice is unspecified rather than wrong.
findings.required_action: Either define the multi-match case in the design/record (e.g. no qualification for AMBIGUOUS, or a label that says which handle the label describes) or state in the docstring that qualification always describes matches[0].

findings.claim: Two non-content failure modes of the new blocking read propagate instead of being absorbed, and the new public label vocabulary is absent from the module's declared public API.
findings.evidence: b06_review_probe.json#claim5_fuzz_conflict_reader#edges: a store whose fetchone raises propagates RuntimeError; a row without the metadata_json column raises KeyError('metadata_json') - the read has no try around fetchone. (Context: with a dict-row store the pre-existing read_prompt_injection_review in the same block fails first with KeyError: 0, so such a store is already unsupported.) resolver.__all__ lists the B03 sentinels but no QUALIFICATION_* constant, and company_wiki/source_catalog/__init__.py does not re-export them either, although the test file imports them by name.
findings.impact: Low: no in-package caller passes such a store, and the constants are reachable by direct import. But the label vocabulary is a cross-repo contract value, so its non-listing weakens the 'this is the public contract' signal that the neighbouring B03 constants already carry.

findings.evidence: b06_review_cfg08_pre.json (config.py swapped to the 728b5e0^ blob on an otherwise identical tree): 'read_only:' -> refused(TypeError, 'read_only must be a boolean'); 'read_only: "false"' -> refused(CatalogConfigError CFG-08); 'reusable_for_filing:' -> accepted with None. models.py:147-148 (unchanged by this commit and present before it) is the source of the TypeError. b06_review_cfg08_head.json: 'read_only:' -> CatalogConfigError('...CFG-08'). The commit message, the new config.py comment and the new test docstring all say the value 'would be stored as None - which is falsy, while the absent field's default is True'. The prior reviewer's finding (reviews/B.VR-b03.json B-VR03-03) described the mechanism correctly, and the disposition row repeats it correctly.
findings.impact: The fix itself is right and matches the annotations (null refused for read_only, null legal for reusable_for_filing); only the justification in the code comment, the test docstring and the commit message is wrong, which is the same class of reason/behaviour mismatch this run has repeatedly flagged (a future reader would conclude the pre-fix path was fail-open).
findings.required_action: Correct the three wordings to what was measured: the admission check let a null through and the config died later with a TypeError from RootSpec.__post_init__ instead of the CatalogConfigError callers handle; the fix normalises the error type to the admission point.
